test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 10 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Two outlet pipes, A and B, can separately empty a full tank in 17 hours and 15 hours, respectively. Both the outlet pipes are opened together for ‘x’ hours. Had outlet pipe B been opened alone, it would have taken (x + 5) hours to empty the same quantity of water from the tank. What is the value of x?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Work done by (A + B) in x hours = Work done by B in (x + 5) hours.

⇒ (EfficiencyA + EfficiencyB) × x = EfficiencyB × (x + 5)

⇒ 15x + 17x = 17x + 85 (Using Efficiency A=15, B=17 from inverse of time)

⇒ 15x = 85 ⇒ x = 85/15 = 17/3 = 5 2/3 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 2/3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by Pipe A = 17 hours

Time taken by Pipe B = 15 hours

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = LCM of individual times; Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

Combined efficiency of A + B = 15 + 17 = 32 units/hr

⇒ Quantity emptied by (A + B) in x hours = 32 × x = 32x units

⇒ Quantity emptied by B alone in (x + 5) hours = 17 × (x + 5) units

⇒ Since the quantity is the same: 32x = 17(x + 5)

⇒ 32x = 17x + 85

⇒ 32x − 17x = 85

⇒ 15x = 85

⇒ x = 85 ÷ 15 = 17 ÷ 3

⇒ x = 5 2/3 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 5 2/3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns

Outlet pipes are considered to do negative work. If an outlet pipe empties a tank in T hours, its efficiency is −1/T per hour.

Efficiency and Time Relationship

The efficiency of a pipe is inversely proportional to the time it takes to fill or empty the tank (Efficiency ∝ 1/Time).

Combined Work Equation

When multiple pipes work together, the total efficiency is the algebraic sum of their individual efficiencies (Net E = E₁ + E₂ + ...).
